What exists now that didn\\u0027t: \\u0060StreamRequestDecision\\u0060 (Domain) holds the whole re-ask rule as a pure function, \\u0060TaskDependencyCatchUp\\u0060 (Connectors) mints dependency asks on landing, \\u0060LedgerTaskLookup\\u0060 (Cli) resolves a task id and project off ledger records, and \\u0060EventCatchUpRequest\\u0060 gained \\u0060SupersededAt\\u0060, \\u0060SupersededByRequestId\\u0060, and \\u0060ForDependencyOfTaskId\\u0060.\\n- The gotcha: \\u0060EventCatchUpRequest.IsOutstanding\\u0060 is now the only correct way to ask \\u0022is this ask live\\u0022. Five sites query the fields directly in LINQ (they can\\u0027t call the property), so any new reader must include \\u0060SupersededAt == null\\u0060 or it will act on a request a human deliberately closed out. That exact miss in \\u0060EventCatchUpInbox\\u0060 was this branch\\u0027s own self-review finding.\\n- Also non-obvious: \\u0060EventCatchUpResponder.AnswerAsync\\u0060 now runs a \\u0060RunListItem\\u0060 query before its scan, so a stream ask costs one extra round trip; and the dependency walk descends only through tasks this node holds, which means a chain of blockers arrives one hop per landing rather than all at once. That\\u0027s deliberate, not a partial implementation.\\n- Left undone on purpose: \\u0060h9k task add --from-issue\\u0060\\u0027s own \\u0060--again\\u0060 still means \\u0022second pr-review adoption\\u0022 and does not supersede a catch-up request; \\u0060h9k task pull --again\\u0060 is the only lever for that. The held-tail ask and the decline bookkeeping moved to the sibling task on automatic completion of held tails, so nothing here retries a dependency after its cooldown expires except the next landing.\\n- One suspicion I could not pin down from this node: the challenge session\\u0027s open question about the Mac\\u0027s 14 run streams answering with tails but no \\u0060RunDispatched\\u0060 is still open. My change makes a task ask carry its runs, which covers the pull path, but if those genesis events really do carry a retired event type name, \\u0060EventScopeRegistry\\u0060 still skips them silently in \\u0060AnswerAsync\\u0060\\u0027s \\u0060InvalidOperationException\\u0060 catch and no amount of asking will bring them over. Checking the event types at version 1 of streams \\u006001a04805-1444-709c-a6ff-ef82a80cd7a3\\u0060 and \\u006001a07d6b-d481-7304-97ea-bdb5229f6a91\\u0060 on the Mac is still the way to settle
